newsitem.title: UK: Dlr steady in Europe, market awaits German budget.
newsitem.headline: Dlr steady in Europe, market awaits German budget.

text.p: The dollar was steady to firmer in morning Europe with dollar/yen bolstered by gains in mark/yen, but dollar/mark kept to ranges above 1.75.

Short covering of marks after Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer's comments Thursday gave the mark a boost late Thursday and overnight but dealers said the impact of the central banker's remarks were beginning to wane in early Europe.

Although soft German data released today was as expected, they provide little interest rate support for the mark and German budget details later today are unlikely to prove an incentive to be long marks, said dealers.

"There is little reason to be bullish of the mark's prospects and today's data helps underline the need for a strong dollar to help German growth," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America in London.
German May retail sales were down a real 2.3 percent year-on-year while June CPI stood at 1.7 percent year/year.
On Thursday, the Bundesbank's Tietmeyer said he wanted the mark strong going into the start of the euro's and that the dollar's corrective phase against the mark was over.
By 0755 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.7544/49 marks against 1.7505/10 marks late Thursday in Europe.

Germany's supplementary 1997 budget and 1998 budget are being discussed by the cabinet in Bonn this morning and Finance Minister Theo Waigel is holding a news conference at 1200 GMT to discuss the results of that meeting.

"A lot of the budget has already been leaked and this will probably soften the blow when they actually confirm the overshoot," said a Japanese bank dealer. "Overall, it shouldn't have too much impact."
Dollar/yen, meantime, was steady after firming overnight on the mark/yen's clearance of key chart resistance. By 0815 GMT, dollar/yen stood at 113.72/82 from 113.03/13 late Thursday.
There was little impact from the upbeat view of Japan's economy in the Economic Planning Agency's monthly report.
There was also little benefit to the yen overnight on news the Philippine central bank effectively devalued the peso, rattling Southeast Asian currency markets.
The yen benefited when the Thai baht was effectively devalued in early July but dealers said there was little evidence of this happening with the Philippine peso move.
Then, dealers said the yen was buoyed by large scale dollar sales by Asian central banks to limit contagion from the currency crisis in Thailand.
Sterling/mark climbed higher in morning Europe, testing above the 2.97 marks level with dealers gearing up for another UK rate rise after Thursday's 25 basis point hike.

Thursday's move initially prompted a sterling sell-off as it came in line with a majority of expectations and disappointed those angling for a bigger rate rise. But inflation is seen persisting and another rise is expected soon, keeping the pound well-supported for now, said dealers.
Sterling/mark stood at 2.9720/30 from 2.9566/76 late Thursday.
